column1: # cases.tsv - the assertions this suite makes, and what each one is called.
# `applies-to` is a space separated list of lanes, or `*` for every lane. It is
# what turns a missing row into a reading: a case that applies to a lane and was
# never reported there is a hole, and until this file existed there was no way to
# tell that from a case nobody had written yet.
# Named lanes and not `*`, because four of the ten run no harness suite at all --
# bsd, kde-live, wayland and macos-netinstall each run one thing, and none of it
# is this. With `*` the grid put a `-` in thirty-three cells for each of them,
# which is noise in the column that is supposed to carry the signal: `-` has to
# mean a lane that was expected to report and did not.
# windows-launch is absent from the walk for a reason that is still open:
# verify-windows.ps1 asserts the same facts and has not been brought onto these
# ids yet, so it reports none of them.
# The ids are dotted and start with the probe family, so a sheet sorts into the
# order somebody reads it in. They are stable across lanes on purpose -- three
# verifiers assert that a window reached 500x400 and until now spelled it three
# different ways, which made one fact look like three to sheetdiff.py.
# The launcher's own walk: neutrinotest.js drives it and verify-linux.sh,
# verify-macos.sh and verify-windows.ps1 each watch it on their own platform.
